title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

errors: The key claim (lieux on a pseudo-disk need an extra boundary-related equivalence/order datum) is stated without argument on this page. The notion of 'pseudo-disque (en un sens convenable)' is not defined, so the claim cannot be checked as stated. It is plausible if lieux are taken up to isotopy rel ∂D, where a contractible region is determined by its pattern of contact with the boundary circle together with its cyclic order.

The reformulated compatibility condition only makes figures behave like cliques if C-disjointness is applied to lieux treated as one-element parts. The passage between elements of L and parts of L (U as a member of a figure vs. U as a subset) is notationally loose here and on p.30.

ideas.what: Figures as families of pairwise C-disjoint lieux; two figures are compatible iff their members pairwise coincide or are disjoint (union is again a figure)
ideas.modern_name: clique/flag complex of a reflexive symmetric 'coherence' relation; cf. coherence spaces, independence complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: coherence spaces: J.-Y. Girard (1987); flag/clique complexes: folklore

ideas.what: Observation that, for pseudo-disks, combinatorial 'lieux' in the interior must carry extra data (equivalence/order linked to the boundary), so a lieu is not just a subset
ideas.modern_name: isotopy classes of subsurfaces rel boundary / combinatorial types encoded by boundary contact pattern (cyclic order on ∂D), as in arc complexes, ribbon graphs, combinatorial maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (arc complexes: Harer, Hatcher; combinatorial maps: Tutte, Cori)

ideas.what: Abandoning point-set interpretation: control structure as abstract (M, ≪ refinement order, R_M compatibility, 𝓕 figures) for 'topologie combinatoire sans points'
ideas.usually_credited_to: locales: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone; tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 announces tame topology but not this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck finds that point-free combinatorial topology of pseudo-disks forces lieux to carry boundary-order/equivalence data. He therefore abandons the 'lieux = subsets, figures = sets of subsets' model for an abstract (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕) axiomatics. This attempt at a combinatorial, pointless foundation of tame topology was never published or developed.
missed.quote: elles doivent être accompagnées d'une donnée supplémentaire, une donnée d'équivalence ou "ordre" lié [...] à ∂D
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete design constraint for any combinatorial or point-free foundation of tame topology, of the kind Grothendieck wanted beyond o-minimality. Regions must be typed by their boundary incidence, as in arc complexes and ribbon-graph combinatorics.

missed.claim: In 1986 the compatibility relation (reflexive, symmetric) with figures as its cliques is essentially Girard's coherence-space structure, enriched with a refinement order. The two settings were not linked in later literature.
missed.quote: C = (M, ≪, R_M, 𝓕 famille de parties de M) ... rel. sym. réfl.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor structural parallel only. It may suggest viewing tame/combinatorial topology data as ordered coherence spaces.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished axiomatics of 'structures de contrôle' for point-free tame topology, with a genuine conceptual turn: lieux need boundary-order data. That is of historical interest, but the page is short and exploratory, and the mathematics is not developed to a result.
transcription_corrections: 'Ainsi Conti dit' should very likely read 'Ainsi Cond. 4 dit' (cf. the margin note on p.30, 'à reformuler cond 4').
'pour U str. ouvert U de F' is probably 'pour tout élément U de F' (figures are sets of parts of L); uncertain.
'dans les "lieux" sur D−∂D ne sont seulement' is probably 'alors les "lieux" sur D−∂D ne sont pas seulement'.
'lié figure-t à ∂D' is probably 'liée à ∂D' / 'lié à la figure ∂D'; uncertain.
'donnée de lieu L des lieux' should be 'donnée d'un ensemble L des lieux'.
